title: Blue Jays erupt for 5 runs in the eighth to beat Red Sox 6-4, extend Boston’s skid to 5
author: The Associated Press
bullets: The Toronto Blue Jays scored five runs in the eighth inning to defeat the Boston Red Sox 6-4.
Willson Contreras hit his 24th home run, but Boston extended their losing streak to five games.
Toronto improved to three consecutive wins, gaining ground in the AL wild-card race, now winning 11 of their last 16.

title: Allston-Brighton residents divided over future of Jackson Mann Community Center, survey shows
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A city survey revealed divided opinions on the Jackson Mann Community Center redevelopment, with options for housing, a school, or both.
The survey received 553 responses; 190 favored housing only, 171 favored a school only, and 124 favored both uses.
Mayor Michelle Wu will decide by year-end; construction won't start until 2030, allowing for program relocation planning.

title: Tour the Patriots’ new 160,000-square-foot training facility
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The New England Patriots unveiled their new 160,000-square-foot New Balance Athletics Center next to Gillette Stadium.
The facility features a 15,000-square-foot weight room, a virtual reality room, and a dining room with made-to-order stations.
The center includes coaches' offices, player lounges, and sophisticated hydrotherapy equipment for player rehabilitation.

title: Man killed in stabbing inside South Station during rush hour, officials say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was fatally stabbed inside Boston's South Station during rush hour Wednesday evening.
Police responded at 5:33 p.m.; the victim died at a hospital after being stabbed on an escalator.
The suspect remains at large; police and investigators are reviewing video and interviewing witnesses.

title: Body found at TD Garden, police say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A body was found Wednesday near TD Garden, reported as an unconscious person at 5:15 p.m.
The deceased was possibly in the parking garage adjacent to TD Garden, police say investigation is ongoing.
Boston police are handling the ongoing investigation, with TD Garden referring all inquiries to them.

title: Athol man charged with child pornography possession
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Kristopher Ambrozewicz, 35, was charged with possession of child sexual abuse materials, according to federal prosecutors.
Authorities seized electronics from Ambrozewicz's home, including laptops and hard drives, for further investigation.
Ambrozewicz, a part-time behavioral health worker, will be arraigned in Worcester Federal Court on Thursday.

title: Police: Person held pregnant woman hostage with gun during dramatic chase on I-93 in Milton
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A pregnant woman was held hostage at gunpoint during a police chase on I-93 in Milton, Massachusetts.
Suspect Dominic Hampton-Boyd, 31, was apprehended after crashing into eight vehicles and fleeing on foot.
The suspect will be arraigned in Quincy District Court; charges and his attorney details are currently unavailable.

title: Stoughton town manager contradicts police chief who accused him of tampering with Sandra Birchmore investigation
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Town Manager Thomas Calter denied interfering with the Sandra Birchmore case investigation after allegations by Police Chief Donna McNamara.
Chief McNamara accused Calter of harassment, discrimination, and pressuring her to resign; Calter called these claims baseless.
Calter and McNamara both remain on paid administrative leave amid ongoing conflict and legal action in Norfolk Superior Court.

title: Nearly 30 people arrested after investigation into drug trafficking in Western Mass.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Twenty-eight people were arrested in Chicopee, Holyoke, and Springfield after a drug trafficking probe named 'Operation Pinky Promise.'
Authorities seized over 12 firearms, more than one kilogram of cocaine, hundreds of fentanyl pills, and heroin during the investigation.
The FBI's Western Massachusetts Gang Task Force led the operation, using surveillance, controlled purchases, and wiretaps for evidence collection.

title: Patriots stock watch 2.0: Who’s rising and falling ahead of preseason opener?
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Romeo Doubs, Drake Maye, and Eli Raridon impressed in recent Patriots practices, boosting their prospects ahead of the preseason opener.
Behren Morton and Jack Westover's roster chances have diminished due to strong performances by teammates and new additions.
Patriots' reserve cornerbacks struggled in scrimmages, highlighting depth concerns without key players Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis.
